meta.source: UN Comtrade monthly HS6 (partner and Kiribati returns)

excluded_lines.reason: One line in Kiribati's return worth more than twice the country's annual GDP. It is kept out of the Kiribati-side totals shown here and reported in this list (see notes); the as-published totals are given alongside.

definitions.other_fish: HS chapter 03 and headings 1604-1605, excluding the tuna codes

notes: categories (Table 2 of the handout, Jan 2025-Jul 2026, 17 months with a Kiribati return): both the recomputed value (partners, kiribati) and the handout value (handout_*) are given. They differ for tuna (97.4 here vs 100.8) and copra (6.5 vs 6.2) because the handout's partner-side category figures came from the 8 Sept data run, before a partner revision to frozen tuna fillets (19.5 -> 16.3); the total (109.7 vs 21.3) is the same in both. Kiribati-side figures agree throughout.

The tuna gap is tuna coded to Kiribati by vessel flag; under balance-of-payments rules much of it may correctly sit outside Kiribati's goods exports. Copra and coconut oil runs the other way: Kiribati records more than partners.

exports/imports.annual: top 15 HS4 headings per year ranked by the larger of the two sides, plus an 'All other' row and a 'Total, all goods' row (is_summary = true). n_partners = number of partner countries that reported the heading that year. annual_months lists the months Kiribati reported; partner values cover those months only.
Partner-reported imports are a lower bound; never compute a trade balance from these tables.
mirror_only_notable: products partners report that Kiribati's own records do not show in the window; hs6 code, number of partners and months given; handout_value is bullet 14 of the handout.

ships_aircraft: Table 4 of the handout recomputed from partners' annual returns (2026: monthly); ships_aircraft_detail has every line of USD 1m or more and the yearly totals with and without Kiribati's own record.
Labels are plain-English shortenings of the HS headings (tracker/hs4_labels.py); where no label is listed the Comtrade description is shortened.

Kiribati's January 2024 import return has one line (HS 940690, prefabricated buildings, USD 3,135m) worth about nine times GDP. It is set aside from the Kiribati-side figures in these tables and listed in meta.excluded_lines; the 9406 row for 2024 shows the remaining value of that heading.

categories.note: Coded to Kiribati by the catching vessel's flag; under balance-of-payments rules much of it may correctly sit outside Kiribati's goods exports. Handout partner figure (100.8) traces to the 8 Sept run (tuna fillets then 19.5, now 16.3 after a partner revision); current data give 97.4.
Mainly sea cucumber and live ornamental fish on the partner side.
Kiribati records more than partners: the method is symmetric. Crude coconut oil (HS 151311): partners 5.7 vs Kiribati 11.9 (handout: 5.4 vs 11.9, 8 Sept run).
HS chapters 72-83; on the partner side almost all scrap iron, aluminium and lead-acid batteries.
Everything else; mostly goods not specified by kind (HS 9999), engine parts, cars and small aircraft on the partner side; cranes on Kiribati's side.
Sum of the five categories above (all goods, including ships and aircraft, which are small on the export side in this window).

Months with no Kiribati return (2025-10) are null on the Kiribati side and are also absent from the partner side of this dataset, which was pulled only for the months Kiribati reported. Partner data are usable about 4 months after the reference month; Thailand's June-July 2026 data were still missing at build time.

ships_aircraft_detail.note: Partner-reported HS 88-89 exported to Kiribati, lines of USD 1m or more. Under BPM6 a vessel or aircraft is a goods import when a resident acquires it, however it is financed. China publishes no monthly data after 2024-12, so its 2025 deliveries cannot be dated by month. Lines before 2022 (e.g. an aircraft from Brazil in 2020, a fishing vessel from Taiwan in 2021) are in lines_1m_plus but not in the handout's Table 4.

rice.note: Viet Nam and Australia do not report rice to Comtrade at HS6 monthly on time, and China and Taiwan have not yet published 2025, so partner data cannot measure rice. Kiribati's own data show rice imports up 40-50 percent in the last year, with suppliers shifting from Australia to Viet Nam, Taiwan and China.
rice.basis: partner_monthly sums every month partners published (all months, not only the months Kiribati reported); kiribati_monthly sums Kiribati's own monthly returns (kiribati_months of 12); *_annual_return are the annual datasets where one exists. Pipeline files are named fish_* but hold this product.

sugar.note: Both sources agree: USD 5-6.5m a year, mostly from Thailand.
